chunks: Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who slandered his wife with adultery, and she is mute, deaf, not hearing what he said. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If she has proof (witnesses), so they testify in the presence of the Imam, he is whipped the legal penalty (Hadd), and they are separated between the two of them, then she is not permissible for him forever; and if there is no proof, so she is prohibited unto him for as long as he stays with her, and there is no sin upon her from him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man slanders his mute wife with adultery and she has no witnesses?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the procedural nuances of *li'an* (mutual imprecation) when the wife is mute and deaf, distinguishing between cases with external witnesses versus those relying on the husband's oath. It highlights the Shia juristic view that if she lacks witnesses, the separation is temporary contingent on cohabitation, contrasting with the permanent separation in the witnessed scenario. This reflects the practical application of Quranic principles in family law, emphasizing the preservation of lineage and marital rights.

en.hubeali: Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a man who slanders his wife with the adultery, and she is mute, deaf, not hearing what he says’ Heasws said: ‘If there was a proof (witnesses) for her, so they can testify in the presence of the Imamasws, he would be whipped the legal penalty (Hadd), and there would be separation between the two of them, then she would not be Permissible for him, forever; and if there does not happen to be proof, so she is Prohibited unto him for whatever he stays with her, and there is no sin upon her from him’.
en.sarwar: 18. Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from abu Basir who has said the following:

“Once abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about the case of a man who accuses his wife of committing fornication and she is speechless, deaf and cannot hear. He (the Imam) said, ‘If she has witnesses who testify before the Imam in her favor, he is whipped as punishment and they are separated from each other. Thereafter she will not be lawful for him in marriage forever. If she does not have witnesses she becomes unlawful for him as long as he stays with her and there is no sin on her because of it.’”
